ruling.recommended_action: Refund SGD 3.07 to the rider by Ryde voucher for the unexcused detour segment (RD-2); no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F7: base $3.90 + distance $30.46 + time $9.10 + waiting $0.11 + platform $1.47 = $45.04), so extra distance is billable and the RD-2 metered branch applies. The code trace settles that one off-route segment exists [F3] and that no traffic incident qualifies under RD-4(a) [F15]; the speed-band record for East Coast Parkway (F12) is at most corroborative, and RD-4(b) does not exempt on its own, so RD-4 gives no relief [F3][F12][F15][RD-4][RD-1].

The live question is the scope of the rider's agreement. Immediately before the detour the driver asked: "Jam on East Coast Parkway is building up ahead, want me to take another way?" [F8], and the rider replied at 09:18: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9]; the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F10]. That message was sent before the segment start (09:20) and is a general route authorisation for the purpose of reaching the destination, not an errand of the driver's own and not a named road [F9][RD-5]. The driver's later statement that "the rider said any faster way was fine, so I went round" [F11] adds nothing: a driver's own post-hoc account is not rider consent (G11), and "went round" is not a rider-named place [F11][RD-5][RD-3].

The agreement exempts the segment only if it is a route chosen to get there [RD-5]. On the measured record it is not: the segment is 4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, lies up to 1027 m off the optimal route, and the trip finished 35.4 min against a 25.2 min estimate [F1][F2][F3]. The route the rider authorised was the one that would be "faster"; the segment chosen did not deliver that, and the whole trip overshot the optimal distance by 12% [F1][F3][RD-5][RD-1]. I therefore read the general authorisation as not covering this segment: the extra kilometres it produced were not the route the rider agreed to. I note openly that the driver's "jam on East Coast Parkway" premise was borne out by the speed-band record [F12]; that is why I read the claim narrowly and keep confidence at 0.7 rather than treating the segment as an obvious driver errand.

The rider also asks me to look at the waiting fee [F5]. On a RydeTAXI trip, stop-and-wait time is charged by the meter's waiting units and is not refundable under RD-3(c); the whole $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min, F4/F5) is meter time and stands [F5][RD-3]. The driver has no upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (F18: route upheld = 0), so RD-6 is not triggered and no account flag is added [F18][RD-6].

Amount (metered refund under RD-2): only the extra km of the unexcused segment is refunded; the flat excess-distance line (F4) is a data artefact and is not used. 2.18 km × $1.4102/km = $3.07424, rounded to $3.07, where $1.4102/km is the trip's distance fare ÷ distance km ($30.46 ÷ 21.60 km) [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. Segment 09:20–09:26: 2.18 km extra, not covered by the general consent or by any incident record → refundable [F3][F8][F9][F12][F15][RD-2][RD-5][RD-1].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver statement [F8][F9][F11]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the exchange is a route discussion ("Jam ... want me to take another way?" / "Just take whichever way is faster lah") and the rider's complaint is about the meter only. Safety concern: none.

segment_findings.reason: F9 (09:18, before the 09:20 segment) answers the driver's F8 question with a general route choice — 'just take whichever way is faster' — which under RD-5 covers only a route chosen to reach the destination. The segment actually driven (4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, up to 1027 m off route, whole trip +2.3 km / 12% and +10.2 min over estimate) was not the faster route the rider authorised, so the extra 2.18 km is not covered by that consent [F1][F2][F3][F8][F9][RD-5][RD-1]. The driver's statement that the rider 'said any faster way was fine, so I went round' [F11] is a post-trip account, not rider consent (G11), though it does evidence a driver-chosen loop rather than a rider-named stop [F11][RD-3]. No traffic incident qualifies under RD-4(a) [F15], so no exemption on that branch.
